# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Morgan Foster**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Ambetter — Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-23**
- **Member:** Morgan Foster
- **Member ID:** W162894592
- **Reference number:** POC-F4C641ED8B-99591
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), State of Illinois
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)* (Date of Last Revision: 04/25) — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lumbar decompression/discectomy (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-23 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria in *Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)* describe what my medical records already document.

Below I have set out the plan's criteria in its own words, followed by the records that correspond to each one.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

The policy states:

> "discectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following:"

**1. Diagnosis of a herniated lumbar disc.** The policy requires:

> "Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc;"

My MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-26 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion.

**2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging.** The policy requires:

> "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

The same MRI of 2026-06-26 shows severe right lateral recess stenosis at L4-L5 with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is imaging confirmation of nerve root compression, at a specific level, on a specific side.

**3. Radiculopathy.** The policy allows this criterion to be met through either a motor or a sensory presentation. One of the options the plan lists is:

> "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

My records document radicular pain into the right calf — pain in a nerve root distribution, on the same side as the imaged compression — along with positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

The policy also provides a motor pathway:

> "R adiculopathy with motor deficit and one of the following:"

with sub-options including:

> "Severe weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by:"
> "a score of ≤ 3 on the Me dical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale, or the inability to ambulate;"

and:

> "Mild to moderate weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by a score of 4 on the Medical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale and one of the following:"
> "Worsening weakness or motor deficit;"

My records note a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level but do not state a numeric Medical Research Council strength grade. If a graded strength examination is documented in my chart, I ask that it be considered as well: [MRC strength score and date, from Dr. Reyes's examination note, if documented].

**4. Failure of conservative therapy within the last year.** The policy requires:

> "Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following:"

> "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

I completed supervised physical therapy — core stabilization and lumbar flexibility — for 12 weeks, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. Twelve weeks exceeds the four weeks the policy asks for.

> "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification;"

[Please complete: dates and description of prescribed activity modification, from Dr. Reyes's office notes or the physical therapy record.] My records do document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and that 24 months of progressive low back pain has not been relieved by rest.

> "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. Six months exceeds the three weeks the policy asks for.

> "2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave approximately 4 weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned. [Please confirm the route and level of the 2026-06-17 injection from the procedure note, so the record matches this criterion precisely.]

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

My symptoms have been present for 24 months and are progressive. I have done the conservative care the policy asks for — physical therapy well beyond four weeks, NSAIDs well beyond three weeks, and a steroid injection — and my pain returned. My MRI identifies a specific, treatable cause: an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis compressing the traversing L5 nerve root, on the same side as my symptoms. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I do not smoke.

The denial notice tells me the request does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria, but it does not identify which criterion in CP.MP.114 my records fail to satisfy. I respectfully ask the reviewer to compare the criteria quoted above, in the plan's own words, against the records in my file.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Ambetter overturn the determination of 2026-08-23 (reference number POC-F4C641ED8B-99591) and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for:

1. A written statement of the specific criterion in *Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)* that my records were found not to meet, and the specific records reviewed;
2. The credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination; and
3. Information about my rights to further appeal, including external review.

**Documents enclosed:** [MRI report dated 2026-06-26], [physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17], [injection procedure note dated 2026-06-17], [Dr. Reyes's office/examination notes], [medication history].

**Deadline and submission:** I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-19**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file through ambetterhealth.com by selecting Illinois and using the state's appeal/grievance form, or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Thank you for taking another look at my file. Please contact me at [phone] or [email] if anything further would help.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Foster**
Member ID: W162894592
Date of birth: [DOB]
[Signature]
[Date]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
